# Recap

## The Setup {.smaller}

Nominal trajectory $\bar{x}_0, \bar{u}_0, \dots, \bar{x}_{T-1}, \bar{u}_{T-1}, \bar{x}_{T}, \bar{u}_{T-1}, \bar{x}_{T}$ satisfies the true nonlinear dynamics.

Define deviations: $\delta x_{t} = x_{t} - \bar{x}_{t}$, $\quad \delta u_{t} = u_{t} - \bar{u}_{t}$.

**Linearized error dynamics** around the nominal:
$$\delta x_{t+1} \approx A_{t}\,\delta x_{t} + B_{t}\,\delta u_{t}, \qquad A_{t} = \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|_{\bar{x}_{t},\bar{u}_{t}}, \quad B_{t} = \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial u}\right|_{\bar{x}_{t},\bar{u}_{t}}$$

**Quadratic cost** (second-order Taylor expansion of $c_{t}$ around nominal):

$$c_{t} \approx \bar{c}_{t} + \begin{bmatrix}q_{t} \\ r_{t}\end{bmatrix}^{\!T} \begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix} + \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix}^{\!T} \begin{bmatrix} Q_t^{cost} & S_t^{\!T} \\ S_t & R_t\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix}$$

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Unlike LQR, the **linear terms** $q_t$ and $r_t$ are generally **nonzero** — the nominal is not yet optimal.
:::

## Backward Pass: Q-function {.smaller}

The Q-function for the deviation problem:

$$\tilde{Q}_{t}(\delta x, \delta u) \approx \text{const} + \begin{bmatrix}Q_x \\ Q_u\end{bmatrix}^{\!T} \begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix} + \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix}^{\!T} \begin{bmatrix}Q_{xx} & Q_{xu} \\ Q_{ux} & Q_{uu}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\delta x \\ \delta u\end{bmatrix}$$

Backward recursion (initialize $V_{T,x} = c_{T,x}$, $V_{T,xx} = c_{T,xx}$):

$$Q_x = q_t + A_{t}^T V_{t+1,x}, \qquad Q_u = r_t + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,x}$$
$$Q_{xx} = c_{t,xx} + A_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} A_{t}, \quad Q_{uu} = c_{t,uu} + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} B_{t}, \quad Q_{ux} = c_{t,ux} + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} A_{t}$$
$$Q_{xx} = Q_t^{cost} + A_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} A_{t}, \quad Q_{uu} = R_t + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} B_{t}, \quad Q_{ux} = S_t + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,xx} A_{t}$$

## Backward Pass: Optimal Gains {.smaller}

Minimize $\tilde{Q}_{t}$ over $\delta u$ (holding $\delta x$ fixed):
$$\frac{\partial \tilde{Q}_{t}}{\partial \,\delta u} = Q_u + Q_{uu}\,\delta u + Q_{ux}\,\delta x = 0$$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
$$\implies \delta u_{t}^* = \underbrace{-Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u}_{k_{t}} + \underbrace{(-Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_{ux})}_{K_{t}}\,\delta x_{t}$$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
| Gain | Expression | Role |
|------|-----------|------|
| $k_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ | $-Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u$ | **Feedforward** — optimization step |
| $K_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ | $-Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_{ux}$ | **Feedback** — state-dependent correction |

Value function updated as: $V_{t,x} = Q_x + Q_{xu} k_{t}$, $\quad V_{t,xx} = Q_{xx} + Q_{xu} K_{t}$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
At the optimum $Q_u = r_t + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,x} = 0$, so $k_{t} = 0$ — identical to LQR.
:::
:::

# Forward Pass

## The Forward Pass Update {.smaller}

Starting from $\hat{x}_0 = \bar{x}_0$, for $t = 0, 1, \dots, T-1$:

$$\boxed{\hat{u}_{t} = \bar{u}_{t} + \alpha\, k_{t} + K_{t}\underbrace{(\hat{x}_{t} - \bar{x}_{t})}_{\delta x_{t}}}$$
$$\hat{x}_{t+1} = f\!\left(\hat{x}_{t},\; \hat{u}_{t}\right) \qquad \leftarrow \text{true nonlinear dynamics}$$

<br>

::: {.callout-warning appearance="minimal"}
**Discussion:** $\alpha$ multiplies $k_{t}$ but **not** $K_{t}$. Shouldn't we scale the entire update $\delta u_{t} = \alpha(k_{t} + K_{t} \delta x_{t})$?
:::

## Why $\alpha$ Scales Only $k_{t}$ {.smaller}

Both $k_{t}$ and $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$ arise from minimizing $\tilde{Q}_{t}$ — both are part of the optimal solution to the linearized sub-problem. The distinction is **open-loop vs. closed-loop**:

| Term | Character | Role |
|------|-----------|------|
| $k_{t} = -Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u$ | **Open-loop** (feedforward) | Depends only on $t$; the search direction |
| $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$ | **Closed-loop** (feedback) | Reacts to whatever $\delta x_{t}$ the nonlinear rollout produces |

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Connection to LQR:** In LQR the full optimal policy is $u_t^* = -K_t x_t$ — the feedback gain IS the solution, not a correction. iLQR adds the feedforward $k_t$ only because $Q_u \neq 0$ off the optimum; at convergence $k_t \to 0$ and only the feedback remains.
:::

## Why $\alpha$ Scales Only $k_{t}$ {.smaller}
::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Why $\alpha$ does not multiply $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$:**

$\alpha$ is a step size along the open-loop search direction $k_{t}$. The closed-loop term $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$ should always be applied at full strength — $\delta x_{t}$ is determined by the nonlinear dynamics, not by how aggressively we step. Scaling it by $\alpha$ would under-correct for nonlinear drift without any line-search benefit.
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
**Special case — linearized forward pass:** if $\delta x_{t}$ propagates through $A_{t} \delta x_{t} + B_{t} \delta u_{t}$, then $\delta x_{t}$ is also a Newton direction and one *could* scale the full pair $\alpha(k_{t} + K_{t} \delta x_{t})$. The nonlinear pass breaks this symmetry, leaving $k_{t}$ as the only clean search direction.
:::

## Thought Experiment {.smaller}

Forward pass: $\hat{u}_{t} = \bar{u}_{t} + \alpha\, k_{t} + K_{t}(\hat{x}_{t} - \bar{x}_{t})$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
**$\alpha = 0$:** $\quad \hat{u}_{t} = \bar{u}_{t} + K_{t}(\hat{x}_{t} - \bar{x}_{t})$

- Feedforward $k_{t}$ is switched off — **no optimization progress**
- $K_{t}$ corrects for nonlinear drift, keeping the trajectory near nominal
- Cost stays approximately the same
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
**$\alpha = 1$:** Full Newton step on the open-loop component.

- $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$ is applied at full strength throughout — its magnitude is set by the nonlinear dynamics, not by $\alpha$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
**At $t = 0$:** $\hat{x}_0 = \bar{x}_0$ always, so $\delta x_0 = 0$.

- The feedback plays **no role at the first step** regardless of $\alpha$
- Only $\alpha k_0$ changes the control there
- Feedback activates only as deviations accumulate along the horizon
:::

# Nonlinear vs. Linearized

## Two Choices for the Forward Pass {.smaller}

|  | **Nonlinear (standard iLQR)** | **Linearized** |
|---|---|---|
| State propagation | $\hat{x}_{t+1} = f(\hat{x}_{t}, \hat{u}_{t})$ | $\delta x_{t+1} = A_{t} \delta x_{t} + B_{t} \delta u_{t}$ |
| Trajectory feasible? | **Yes** — on true dynamics | No — satisfies only linear model |
| Is $\delta x_{t}$ a Newton direction? | No — nonlinear residuals corrupt it | Yes |
| $\alpha$ appropriately scales | Only $k_{t}$ | Full $\alpha(k_{t} + K_{t} \delta x_{t})$ |
| Best suited for | Highly nonlinear systems | Near-optimal, mildly nonlinear |

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Near convergence, linearization error $\to 0$ and the two approaches become equivalent. The difference matters most in the early iterations.
:::
:::

# Line Search

## Backtracking Line Search {.smaller}

**Goal:** find $\alpha \in (0, 1]$ such that the updated trajectory strictly reduces cost.

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Algorithm:**

1. Set $\alpha = 1$
2. Run nonlinear forward pass with current $\alpha$; evaluate $J(\hat{u})$
3. If $J(\hat{u}) < J(\bar{u})$: **accept**, update $\bar{x} \leftarrow \hat{x}$, $\bar{u} \leftarrow \hat{u}$
4. Else: $\alpha \leftarrow \alpha/2$, repeat from step 2
5. After 50 halvings: if $\alpha < 2\times 10^{-6}$, declare convergence
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
```python
alpha = 1.0
for _ in range(50):
    for t in range(T):
        delta_u = K[t] @ (x_new[t] - x_nom[t]) + alpha * k_ff[t]
        u_new[t] = u_nom[t] + delta_u
        x_new[t+1] = f(x_new[t], u_new[t])   # nonlinear step
    if new_cost < current_cost:
        break
    alpha *= 0.5
```
:::

## Predicted Cost Improvement {.smaller}

The backward pass implicitly computes the predicted improvement:

$$\Delta J = \sum_{k=0}^{T-1}\left(Q_u^T k_{t} + \frac{1}{2} k_{t}^T Q_{uu} k_{t}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1} k_{t}^T Q_{uu} k_{t} \;\leq\; 0$$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
This motivates a stronger **Armijo condition**:

$$J(\hat{u}) < J(\bar{u}) - \gamma\,\alpha\,|\Delta J|, \qquad \gamma \in (0,1)$$

Actual decrease must be at least a fraction $\gamma$ of the quadratic model's prediction.
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**At convergence:** $k_{t} \to 0$ (because $Q_u \to 0$), so $\Delta J \to 0$ and $\alpha = 1$ is accepted immediately on the first try — the line search costs nothing.
:::
:::

## Exercise: Optimality at Convergence {.smaller}

At convergence, $k_{t} = -Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u \to 0$, which means:

$$Q_u = r_t + B_{t}^T V_{t+1,x} = 0 \quad \text{for all } t$$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Question:** Write out what this says in terms of the original cost and dynamics.  What classical optimality condition does it correspond to?
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
**Answer:** This is the discrete-time **Pontryagin Maximum Principle** stationarity condition:

$$\frac{\partial c_{t}}{\partial u_{t}} + B_{t}^T \lambda_{t+1} = 0, \qquad \lambda_{t+1} = V_{t+1,x}$$

where $\lambda_{t}$ is the **costate** (adjoint variable). iLQR converges precisely when the KKT conditions are satisfied.
:::

# Full Algorithm

## iLQR: Complete Algorithm {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}
### iLQR

**Input:** initial controls $\bar{u}_{0:T-1}$, dynamics $f_{t}$, costs $c_{t}$, $c_{T}$

**1. Rollout:** simulate $\bar{x}_{t+1} = f_{t}(\bar{x}_{t}, \bar{u}_{t})$ to obtain the nominal trajectory.

**2. Repeat until convergence:**

**2a. Backward pass** — init $V_{T,x} = c_{T,x}$, $V_{T,xx} = c_{T,xx}$; for $t = T-1, \dots, 0$:

- Compute Jacobians $A_{t}, B_{t}$ and cost derivatives at $(\bar{x}_{t}, \bar{u}_{t})$
- Compute $Q_x, Q_u, Q_{xx}, Q_{uu}, Q_{ux}$ via the recursion
- Gains: $k_{t} = -Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u$, $\quad K_{t} = -Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_{ux}$
- Update: $V_{t,x} = Q_x + Q_{xu} k_{t}$, $\quad V_{t,xx} = Q_{xx} + Q_{xu} K_{t}$

**2b. Forward pass** — from $\hat{x}_0 = \bar{x}_0$, simulate with $\hat{u}_{t} = \bar{u}_{t} + \alpha k_{t} + K_{t}(\hat{x}_{t} - \bar{x}_{t})$

**2c. Line search** — if $J(\hat{u}) < J(\bar{u})$: accept; else $\alpha \leftarrow \alpha/2$, repeat 2b

**2d. Update** — $\bar{x}_{t} \leftarrow \hat{x}_{t}$, $\;\bar{u}_{t} \leftarrow \hat{u}_{t}$
:::

## iLQR vs. LQR {.smaller}

| Quantity | LQR | iLQR (per iteration) |
|----------|-----|---------------------|
| Dynamics | $A_{t} x_{t} + B_{t} u_{t}$ | $\bar{x}_{t+1} + A_{t} \delta x_{t} + B_{t} \delta u_{t}$ |
| Cost | Quadratic in $(x, u)$ | Quadratic in $(\delta x, \delta u)$; linear terms nonzero |
| $Q_{uu}$ | $R + B^T P B$ | $c_{uu} + B^T V_{xx} B$ |
| Optimal control | $u^* = -K x$ | $\delta u^* = k + K \delta x$ |
| Feedforward | None ($Q_u = 0$ at optimum) | $k = -Q_{uu}^{-1} Q_u$ (drives improvement) |
| Hessian recursion | Discrete Riccati equation | Same Schur complement form |

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
The backward pass is **structurally identical to LQR** applied to the deviation problem. The only additions: (1) feedforward gains $k_{t}$ from nonzero cost gradients; (2) re-linearize each iteration.
:::
:::

# Extensions

## Beyond iLQR {.smaller}

**Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP):**

iLQR uses only first-order Jacobians of $f_{t}$. DDP adds second-order terms:

$$Q_{xx} \mathrel{+}= \sum_i (V_{t+1,x})^{(i)} f_{t,xx}^{(i)}, \quad Q_{uu} \mathrel{+}= \cdots, \quad Q_{ux} \mathrel{+}= \cdots$$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
- Terms scale as $\mathcal{O}(\|V_{t+1,x}\|)$ — vanish near the optimum where $V_{t+1,x} \to 0$
- Better convergence rate far from the optimum; expensive and rarely used in practice
- iLQR is sometimes called **Gauss-Newton DDP**
:::

## Beyond iLQR {.smaller}
**Natural extensions:**

| Extension | Idea |
|-----------|------|
| Constrained iLQR | Handle $u_{t} \in \mathcal{U}$ via augmented Lagrangian (AL-iLQR) |
| MPC | Re-solve at each timestep with a receding horizon |
| Warm-starting | Initialize next solve from the shifted previous solution |

# Summary

## Summary {.smaller}

**Forward pass update:**
$$\hat{u}_{t} = \bar{u}_{t} + \alpha\, k_{t} + K_{t}(\hat{x}_{t} - \bar{x}_{t}), \qquad \hat{x}_{t+1} = f(\hat{x}_{t}, \hat{u}_{t})$$

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
- $\alpha$ scales only $k_{t}$ — the Newton search direction in $u$
- $K_{t} \delta x_{t}$ corrects for nonlinear drift; it is not a search direction unless dynamics are linear
- Using nonlinear dynamics keeps the trajectory **feasible** at every iteration
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
**Line search:** halve $\alpha$ until $J$ decreases; $k_{t} \to 0$ signals convergence

**Convergence ↔ optimality:** $Q_u = 0$ is the discrete-time PMP stationarity condition

**DDP vs. iLQR:** dynamics Hessian terms improve convergence rate but are rarely worth the cost
:::

## Summary {.smaller}

**Computational complexity per iteration:**

| Step | Cost |
|------|------|
| Backward pass | $\mathcal{O}(T(n^3 + m^3))$ — matrix inversions dominate |
| Forward pass (per line-search trial) | $\mathcal{O}(T \cdot \text{cost of } f)$ |
| Iterations to convergence | Typically 10–100 for smooth problems |
